chunks: From him, from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both), who said:

I asked him about the found object (luqatah). He said: 'Do not pick it up. If you are tested (i.e., if you pick it up), then announce it for one year. If its owner comes, then return it; otherwise, place it among the breadth of your wealth, so that what applies to your wealth applies to it, until a claimant comes for it.'
He said: And I asked him about silver coins found in a house. He said: 'If the house is inhabited, they belong to its people; and if it is ruined, you are more entitled to what you found.'

key_terms.اللُّقَطَة: Found object or lost property picked up from the ground
key_terms.عُرْضِ مَالِكَ: The breadth/extent of your wealth (integrated into personal assets)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling for found money or items (Luqatah) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) details the jurisprudence of *luqatah* (found property), distinguishing between general items and specific currency like silver coins (*wariq*). The ruling for coins hinges on the state of the dwelling: if inhabited, they belong to the residents; if ruined, the finder has priority, reflecting the Shia legal principle of preserving wealth while ensuring potential owners have a reasonable window to reclaim their property.
